The new policy document changes something the spec already treated as settled, so I'm reopening it: the v2 snapshot is preserved to history before editing, and this becomes v3.

What changed: D1 (30-day retention) is superseded. The binding internal policy caps this dataset's identifiable-record retention at 7 days, the dataset has no copies elsewhere to reconcile, and you've confirmed you can't waive it even though you own the implementation — so this isn't a discretionary choice anymore, it's an observed hard limit. R1 now targets 7 days, with boundary tests at day 6 (retained) and day 8 (purged), mirroring the day 29/31 pattern you used for the 30-day version.

On timing: you said the policy takes effect at the first scheduled purge after deployment, with no separate migration, immediate purge, or backlog deadline. That lines up with the existing implementation behavior already on record — the job re-evaluates *every* record against the current parameter on each run, not just new ones. So the very next scheduled purge after you deploy the 7-day parameter will automatically catch any 8–29-day-old records still sitting in the dataset under the old policy, with no extra backlog job needed. I've recorded that as its own requirement (R3) so it isn't lost as an implicit side effect.

D2 (preserve existing purge logic and deployment process, change only the parameter and its boundary tests) is untouched — this new policy doesn't ask you to change mechanism, just the number and its effective-date behavior. I also tightened the authority language: the executor still can't move the duration or touch purge/deployment mechanics without a new decision, and now explicitly can't waive the 7-day cap either, since that's policy rather than your call to relax.

Nothing here is left open — the policy, the dataset's isolation, the effective-date mechanics, and the authority limits are all pinned down by what you've given me, so I'm re-freezing at v3 and moving straight into planning rather than pausing to ask something that's already answered.

# Internal dataset retention

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v3
Frozen: true
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Problem Statement

Keep a bounded investigation history in the existing internal dataset, now bounded by a binding internal policy cap rather than pure owner discretion.

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Retain for 30 days | Decided: owner previously chose 30 days | Superseded by D3 — see Decision History | superseded |
| D2 | Keep existing purge implementation and deployment process; change only the retention parameter and its boundary tests | Decided: owner's settled scope | None | resolved |
| D3 | Retain identifiable records for 7 days | Observed: newly supplied binding internal policy caps this dataset's identifiable-record retention at 7 days; dataset has no copies in other stores, so no cross-store reconciliation is needed. Decided: owner confirmed the policy is binding and cannot be waived even though the owner controls the implementation. | None — the cap is mandatory, not a discretionary tradeoff | resolved |
| D4 | New parameter takes effect at the first scheduled purge after the existing approved deployment process; no separate migration, immediate one-off purge, or backlog deadline is required | Decided: owner's explicit instruction. Observed: existing purge job re-evaluates every record against the current parameter on each scheduled run, so the first post-deployment run will apply the 7-day cutoff to all existing records (including any 8–29-day-old backlog) without a dedicated migration job. | None — the mechanism already satisfies the stated effective-date requirement | resolved |

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Set the existing purge parameter to 7 days | Parameter is 7; day 6 remains and day 8 is purged | D3 |
| R2 | Preserve purge logic and deployment process | Diff contains only parameter and boundary-test updates | D2 |
| R3 | New parameter takes effect via the first scheduled purge after deployment, with no separate migration or backlog job | After deployment, the next scheduled purge run purges all identifiable records older than 7 days — including previously-retained 8–29-day-old records — using the existing per-run re-evaluation logic; no additional one-time job is introduced | D4 |

## Constraints and Authority

Only this dataset is in scope. Executor may choose edit mechanics; cannot change the retention duration below or above 7 days, or alter purge/deployment behavior, without a new decision. The 7-day cap is a binding internal policy: the owner controls the implementation but has no authority to waive or relax it. No broader rollout is authorized. The prior 30-day choice was legitimate when made and is not being treated as an error — it is being superseded by a new binding constraint effective going forward.

## Validation Contract

Run the existing purge tests with the parameter set to 7 and updated boundary fixtures (day 6 remains, day 8 purged); inspect the diff for R2. Additionally confirm R3: after deployment, verify the first scheduled purge run purges any remaining 8–29-day-old records via the existing re-evaluation logic, with no separate migration job present in the diff. Unexpected retention, early deletion, a missed backlog purge on the first post-deployment run, or out-of-scope changes fail validation. Check after the edit and after the first post-deployment scheduled run. A failed check requires correction before completion.

## Decision History

- D1 ("Retain for 30 days"; Basis: Decided: owner previously chose 30 days; resolved) — superseded by D3. Reason: a newly supplied binding internal policy caps this dataset's identifiable-record retention at 7 days, and the owner cannot waive it. The 30-day decision remains a legitimate historical choice for the period before this policy applied; it no longer governs going forward.
- Reopen event: Specification Version incremented v2 → v3; Frozen set false then re-set true within this turn once the new policy fully resolved the only affected decision. Trigger: newly supplied binding internal policy document. Affected decisions: D1 (superseded by D3); added D4 to capture the effective-date mechanics the owner specified. D2 was reviewed and found unaffected. The pre-edit v2 spec was preserved to `history/spec-v2-<reopen-timestamp>.md` before this edit per reopen semantics.

## Critique Reconciliation

None.

## Ambiguities

No blocking decisions remain. The retention duration, its effective-date mechanism, dataset isolation, and authority limits are all settled by the supplied policy and the owner's confirmation that it cannot be waived.

responses.reply: This matches what's already locked into v3 exactly — the 7-day parameter, the day-6-remains/day-8-purged boundary, D2 kept untouched (only parameter and boundary tests change), D1 preserved with its supersession reason in Decision History, and R3 confirming the existing per-run purge logic already handles the backlog with no separate migration job or extra feature. There's nothing new to incorporate, so the spec stays at v3, Validated and Frozen, with no reopening or version bump needed. Moving straight into planning now.
